newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak SAX continues downtrend on weak blue chips.
newsitem.headline: Slovak SAX continues downtrend on weak blue chips.

text.p: Major Slovak shares were mixed in thinner trading on the Bratislava Stock Exchange (BSE) on Thursday, with losses to several blue chips pulling the SAX index further down.
Commercial bank VUB fell 85 to close at 1,595 crowns as the SAX index closed down 1.45 points to 195.45.
But thin volumes -- only four shares of VUB changed hands on the automated floor -- was too little to indicate any longer-term trend, brokers said.
Steel maker VSZ again led trading on the BSE floor, trading 3,168 shares and closed down four crowns at 741.

"We don't expect significant movements in VSZ's price until the company's general annual meeting later this month, but we think it may move slightly higher in the coming days," said Bohus Betko of ING Barings.
Brokers said sluggish trading and minor price moves were also due to caution ahead of upcoming annual meetings.
"But we expect more lively trading to start shortly before the annual meetings season, which is just to come at the and of this month and the beginning of May," he added.
Overall volume rose to 351,350 shares, boosted mainly by direct trades where 344,529 stocks were traded, from 190,189 shares matched on Wednesday.
Turnover increased to 185.26 million crowns from 156.60 million on Wednesday.
